newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan opposition leaders meet in Eritrea.
newsitem.headline: Sudan opposition leaders meet in Eritrea.

text.p: The leaders of Sudan's military and political opposition began a strategy meeting in Eritrea on Thursday, an opposition official said.
All the leaders of the NDA (National Democratic Alliance), the coalition trying to oust the Islamist government in Khartoum, were present, the NDA official told Reuters.

He said they included NDA chairman Moulana al-Mirghani, John Garang, leader of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), former Prime Minister Sadiq al-Mahdi, who escaped Khartoum last December, Abdul Aziz Khalid of the Sudanese Alliance Forces and NDA's secretary-general Mubarak Al-Mahdi.

The NDA has its headquarters in Asmara, the Eritrean capital. Eritrea, Sudan's small but militarily powerful eastern neighbour, backs the opposition but denies its army is taking part in the fighting.
The SPLA has claimed a string of battlefield successes in southern Sudan and the NDA says coalition forces are active in several other regions.
The last NDA leadership meeting was in Asmara in March.
At that time Sadiq al-Mahdi's position in the opposition had not yet been decided and he was not formally a NDA member.
But al-Mahdi attended on Thursday as a member.
The official declined to divulge the agenda of the meeting, whose start has been delayed several times, but said it would probably last until Saturday.
